column1: When did President Tinubu declare a food security emergency?
column2: On 13 July 2023, just weeks after taking office, making food production a top national priority.
column3: It shows food prices were treated as an emergency from the start.

column1: How many farmers got seeds, fertiliser and inputs under NAGS-AP?
column2: 634,043 farmers, through about 600 input dealers, using digital registration to target real farmers.
column3: Support went straight to farmers, not middlemen.

column1: How much food did the NAGS-AP programme help produce?
column2: About 2.54 million tonnes of produce worth an estimated ₦2.31 trillion across four farming seasons.
column3: More food grown at home helps bring prices down over time.

column1: How much of its own wheat does Nigeria now grow?
column2: About 10% in 2024, up from under 3% in 2023, after the harvested wheat area rose roughly 300% in the first year.
column3: Less imported wheat means bread and flour depend less on the dollar.

column1: What new funding did NAGS-AP win in February 2026?
column2: A further US$200 million from the African Development Bank for a four-year Phase II.
column3: International lenders backing the programme is a sign it's working.

column1: How many tractors are being rolled out to farmers?
column2: Over 2,000 tractors, plus combine harvesters, 9,000 implements and mobile workshops. The rollout began in February 2026, led by the Bank of Agriculture.
column3: Farmers can hire machines through service providers instead of farming by hand.

column1: What new ministry did the President create for herders and livestock?
column2: The Federal Ministry of Livestock Development, created on 9 July 2024, the first dedicated livestock ministry.
column3: Modern ranching is key to reducing farmer-herder clashes.

column1: How much agricultural lending did NIRSAL guarantee in 2025?
column2: Over ₦100 billion in approved credit guarantees, making it easier for banks to lend to farmers and agribusinesses.
column3: Farmers who could never get a bank loan can now access credit.

column1: Which agency came first out of 36 in a national reform ranking?
column2: The Nigeria Agricultural Quarantine Service scored 100% in PEBEC's 2024 regulatory reform assessment, ranking first of 36 agencies.
column3: Faster export certification helps Nigerian farmers sell abroad.

column1: What new export deal did Nigeria sign with China in 2026?
column2: An export protocol for wild aquatic products (13 August 2026), opening the Chinese market to eligible Nigerian exporters.
column3: New markets mean more income for fishermen and exporters.
